concerns.text: FR-006 (paired t-test on reconstruction errors across 50 degraded test scenes) is anchored '(See US-2)', but US-2 is the structural-property/correlation story; the paired t-test on the deterministic-vs-diffusion performance gap belongs to US-3 (whose journey explicitly covers comparative benchmarking). Cross-reference mismatch.

FR-007 (sensitivity analysis of the filter's cutoffs) is anchored '(See US-2)', but it concerns the US-1/US-3 filter parameters, not US-2's spectral analysis. Also 'false-positive/negative rates' is inconsistent terminology for a regression/denoising task measured by Chamfer Distance — no FR or SC defines a classification decision these rates would apply to.

FR-007 defers the sweep values ('k ∈ {representative low, medium, and high values}') while SC-004 pins concrete values 'k ∈ {5, 10, 15}'. Pick one convention so the FR and its success criterion describe the same sweep.

'a Chamfer Distance that is no more than 1.18x (approx. [deferred] efficiency)' mixes a hard-coded ratio (1.18x) with a [deferred] marker in the same clause. The 1.18x is a pre-asserted empirical threshold that contradicts the deferred-value convention stated in the Measurable Outcomes preamble; state the metric and reference (baseline CD) and defer the ratio.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-2 Acceptance Scenario 2 vs Edge Cases
concerns.text: US-2 scenario 2 mandates 'identifies at least one specific eigenmode... statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05)', while the Edge Cases section requires the system to 'flag the hypothesis as unsupported and record the null result' when no significant correlation exists. These are compatible only if the acceptance scenario is reframed as measuring the correlation (per SC-005) rather than guaranteeing a positive finding; as written the scenario asserts an empirical outcome.
Dataset is named 'Depth Anything 3 (DA3)' in the first assumption but 'the DA dataset' in the third assumption. Use one name consistently.
